front_line: The mall in your pocket. Watching the margin slope
thesis: DoorDash is really two businesses on one ticker: a dominant restaurant duopoly that prints cash, with a near-100%-margin ad engine bolted on top that lifts blended margins mechanically. The business is ownable and the moat is real, but at 41x FCF the price already assumes both the ad compounding and the grocery land-grab win. A soft Aug 4 print that re-rates toward the base case is the entry where the asymmetry finally points up.
moat: Strong local network moat in restaurants; near-zero moat in the grocery category driving growth.
risks: EPS fell four straight quarters; the "margin slope" the memo flags comes with no disclosed number.

categories.label: Valuation
categories.note: Means upside is more dependent on execution

drafts.x_post: DASH is two businesses wearing one ticker: a cash-printing restaurant fortress with a near-zero-cost ad engine on top. Great business, demanding price at 41x FCF. The split nobody discloses decides everything — Aug 4 is the tell. Dead Simple Score: 80. Watching.
video_talking_points: DoorDash runs the app you open for food — and now groceries, alcohol, and retail.
At 41x free cash flow it trades 28% above its own base case, priced for two unproven bets to both win.
The bull case: a dominant restaurant duopoly that prints cash, with a near-100%-margin ad engine on top that lifts blended margins mechanically — even if grocery never works.
The main risk: EPS fell four straight quarters and the company won't disclose the restaurant-versus-grocery split that resolves the whole thesis.
Verdict: ownable business, real moat, wrong price — watch for Aug 4 to show stable restaurant margin and 20%+ ad growth.
Let the feared bad quarter be the entry where the asymmetry finally points up.
